# API contract

All endpoints live under `/api`, take and return JSON (except the Export workbook), and need `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` (except `/api/health*`).

## Ports (Docker Compose)

| Service | Host port | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| frontend (nginx) | 8080 | serves the UI, forwards `/api` to the backend |
| backend | 8081 | Spring Boot; also reachable directly for API tests |
| auth (Firebase Auth Emulator) | 9099 | used by default; project id `demo-contacts` |
| db (PostgreSQL 16) | not published | volume `db-data` |

## Errors

Every error body is a list of field errors:

```json
{ "errors": [ { "field": "email", "message": "must be a valid email" } ] }
```

`field` is `null` for errors that belong to no field. Status codes:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | validation error; `field` names the offending field (`name`, `email`, `attributes[2].key`, `tags[0]`, ...) |
| 401 | missing, malformed, expired or foreign token |
| 403 | the caller's Role does not allow the action |
| 404 | not found, **or the caller is not a Member** (identical body: `{"errors":[{"field":null,"message":"not found"}]}`) |
| 409 | outdated `version`, duplicate Member, last Owner, Tag name taken, purge of an active Contact, Restore of a stale Revision |
| 413 | request body larger than 1 MB |
| 429 | rate limit (per User, default 300 requests per minute) |

## User

`GET /api/me` → 200 `{ id, email, emailVerified, displayName }`. Creates the User on first call, updates email, verified flag and display name from the token on every call, and activates pending invitations for a verified email.

## Workspaces

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces` | any User | | 200 `[{ id, name, role }]` sorted by name |
| `POST /api/workspaces` | any User | `{ name }` (1–100 chars after trimming) | 201 `{ id, name, role: "OWNER" }` |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Member | | 200 `{ id, name, role }` |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Owner | `{ name }` | 200 `{ id, name, role }` |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}` | Owner | `{ confirmName }` (must equal the name exactly, else 400 `confirmName`) | 204 |

Roles: `OWNER`, `EDITOR`, `VIEWER`.

## Members and invitations

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/members` | Member | | 200 `{ members: [{ userId, email, displayName, role }], invitations: [{ id, email, role, createdAt }] }` |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/members` | Owner | `{ email, role }` | 201 `{ status: "MEMBER", member: {...} }` for a verified existing User, otherwise 201 `{ status: "INVITED", invitation: {...} }`; 409 if already a Member or invited |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}/members/{userId}` | Owner | `{ role }` | 200 member; 409 when it would leave no Owner |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/members/{userId}` | Owner, or the Member themself (leave) | | 204; 409 when it would leave no Owner |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/invitations/{id}` | Owner | | 204 |

## Contacts

Contact body:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid", "version": 3, "deleted": false, "mergedInto": null,
  "firstName": "Saša", "lastName": "Novak", "email": "sasa@example.si", "phone": "+386 41 123 456",
  "company": "Podjetje d.o.o.", "jobTitle": "Vodja", "street": "Slovenska 1", "postalCode": "1000",
  "city": "Ljubljana", "country": "SI", "note": "...",
  "attributes": [ { "key": "kompetenca", "value": "spletnoProgramiranje" } ],
  "tags": [ "udelezenec2025" ],
  "createdAt": "...", "updatedAt": "..."
}
```

Field rules: values are trimmed, a blank value becomes `null`. At least one of `firstName`, `lastName`, `email` (400, field `firstName`). Maximum lengths: `firstName`, `lastName`, `city` 100; `email` 254 (must be a valid address); `phone` 50; `company`, `jobTitle`, `street` 200; `postalCode` 20; `note` 2000. `country` is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, stored in upper case.

Attributes: at most 100; `key` matches `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,49}$`, unique on the Contact ignoring case, not equal (ignoring case) to a Predefined field name, `id` or `tags`; `value` 1–500 characters after trimming. Order is kept. Errors name `attributes[i].key` / `attributes[i].value`.

Tags: at most 50 per Contact; each 1–50 characters with no whitespace; no repeats on one Contact ignoring case (errors name `tags[i]`). A new Tag is created on first use; an existing one is reused regardless of case and keeps its first spelling.

| Method and path | Role | Body / query | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts` | Member | query below | 200 `{ items: [Contact], total, page, size }` |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts` | Editor | Contact fields, `attributes`, `tags` | 201 Contact + `possibleDuplicates: [{ id, firstName, lastName, email, phone, matchKinds }]` |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Member | | 200 Contact (also a Deleted contact) |
| `PUT /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Editor | `version` + all fields | 200 Contact + `possibleDuplicates`; 409 on outdated `version` |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}?version=n` | Editor | (`version` optional) | 204, writes a `DELETE` Revision |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/restore` | Editor | | 200 Contact; restores a Deleted contact with its last state (`RESTORE` Revision); 409 if not deleted |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/purge` | Owner | | 204; permanently removes a Deleted contact and its Revisions; 409 for an active Contact |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions` | Member | | 200 `[Revision]` newest first |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions/{n}/restore` | Editor | `{ version }` | 200 Contact; writes a `RESTORE` Revision equal to Revision n; 409 on outdated version or for a Deleted contact |

List query: `q` (search text, case and diacritic insensitive, over first name, last name, full name, email, phone, company, city), `tag` (repeatable), `tagMode=all|any` (default `all`), `attr` (repeatable, `key=value` matches value case-insensitively, `key` alone means presence), `country`, `company` (case-insensitive equality), `deleted=true` (Deleted contacts only; default active only), `sort=lastName|firstName|company|updatedAt` (default `lastName`), `dir=asc|desc` (default `asc`, `desc` for `updatedAt`), `page` (from 0), `size` (1–100, default 20; above 100 → 400 `size`).

Revision: `{ number, type, author: { id, email, displayName }, createdAt, state: { firstName, ..., note, attributes, tags, deleted, mergedInto } }`. Types: `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `RESTORE`, `MERGE`, `MERGED_AWAY`. No endpoint changes or deletes a Revision (only purge and Workspace deletion remove them with their Contact).

## Tags

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags` | Member | | 200 `[{ name, count }]` sorted by name; `count` = active Contacts |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | `{ name }` | 200 `{ name, count }`; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact; 409 if the new name exists (any case, other Tag) |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | | 204; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact |

`{name}` is matched ignoring case.

## Duplicate sets

`GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/duplicate-sets` (Member) → 200 `[{ contacts: [Contact], matches: [{ contactIds: [a, b], kind: "EMAIL" | "PHONE" | "NAME", value }] }]`.

Normalisation: email lower case; phone `00`→`+`, then digits only, at least 6 digits; full name = first + last name, lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed (both names needed). Active Contacts only, grouped transitively.

## Merge

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/merge` (Editor)

```json
{
  "survivorId": "uuid",
  "contacts": [ { "id": "uuid", "version": 2 }, { "id": "uuid", "version": 5 } ],
  "fieldSources": { "email": "uuid-of-source" },
  "attributeSources": { "kompetenca": "uuid-of-source" }
}
```

2–10 distinct active Contacts; the Survivor and every source must be among them (400 otherwise). For a field without a chosen source the Survivor's value is kept, or the first non-empty value in list order when the Survivor has none. Attributes are combined by key (ignoring case); the Survivor's value wins unless `attributeSources` names another Contact. Tags are combined. The others become Deleted contacts with `mergedInto` = Survivor and a `MERGED_AWAY` Revision; the Survivor gets a `MERGE` Revision. Any outdated version → 409 and nothing changes. Response 200: the Survivor.

## Export

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/export` (Member) with exactly one of:

- `{ "contactIds": ["uuid", ...] }`: those Contacts, in list default order (last name, first name); a Deleted, foreign or unknown id → 400 `contactIds`;
- `{ "filter": { q, tag, tagMode, attr, country, company, sort, dir } }`: every active Contact matching, in the filter's order.

Both or neither → 400. More than 10,000 Contacts → 400. Response 200 `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<workspace-name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx"` (name reduced to letters, digits, `-` and `_`).

Columns, in order: `Ime`, `Priimek`, `E-pošta`, `Telefon`, `Podjetje`, `Delovno mesto`, `Ulica`, `Poštna številka`, `Kraj`, `Država`, `Opomba`, `Oznake` (Tags joined by `, `), then one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted). Every cell is a text cell; values are never formulas.

## Health

`GET /api/health` (liveness) and `GET /api/health/ready` (readiness, checks the database), no token needed.

| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Member | | 200 Contact (also a Deleted contact) |
| `PUT /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}` | Editor | `version` + all fields | 200 Contact + `possibleDuplicates`; 409 on outdated `version` |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}?version=n` | Editor | (`version` optional) | 204, writes a `DELETE` Revision |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/restore` | Editor | | 200 Contact; restores a Deleted contact with its last state (`RESTORE` Revision); 409 if not deleted |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/purge` | Owner | | 204; permanently removes a Deleted contact and its Revisions; 409 for an active Contact |
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions` | Member | | 200 `[Revision]` newest first |
| `POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts/{cid}/revisions/{n}/restore` | Editor | `{ version }` | 200 Contact; writes a `RESTORE` Revision equal to Revision n; 409 on outdated version or for a Deleted contact |

List query: `q` (search text, case and diacritic insensitive, over first name, last name, full name, email, phone, company, city), `tag` (repeatable), `tagMode=all|any` (default `all`), `attr` (repeatable, `key=value` matches value case-insensitively, `key` alone means presence), `country`, `company` (case-insensitive equality), `deleted=true` (Deleted contacts only; default active only), `sort=lastName|firstName|company|updatedAt` (default `lastName`), `dir=asc|desc` (default `asc`, `desc` for `updatedAt`), `page` (from 0), `size` (1–100, default 20; above 100 → 400 `size`).

Revision: `{ number, type, author: { id, email, displayName }, createdAt, state: { firstName, ..., note, attributes, tags, deleted, mergedInto } }`. Types: `CREATE`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `RESTORE`, `MERGE`, `MERGED_AWAY`. No endpoint changes or deletes a Revision (only purge and Workspace deletion remove them with their Contact).

## Tags

| Method and path | Role | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags` | Member | | 200 `[{ name, count }]` sorted by name; `count` = active Contacts |
| `PATCH /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | `{ name }` | 200 `{ name, count }`; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact; 409 if the new name exists (any case, other Tag) |
| `DELETE /api/workspaces/{wid}/tags/{name}` | Editor | | 204; `UPDATE` Revision on every affected Contact |

`{name}` is matched ignoring case.

## Duplicate sets

`GET /api/workspaces/{wid}/duplicate-sets` (Member) → 200 `[{ contacts: [Contact], matches: [{ contactIds: [a, b], kind: "EMAIL" | "PHONE" | "NAME", value }] }]`.

Normalisation: email lower case; phone `00`→`+`, then digits only, at least 6 digits; full name = first + last name, lower case, diacritics removed, whitespace collapsed (both names needed). Active Contacts only, grouped transitively.

## Merge

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/merge` (Editor)

```json
{
  "survivorId": "uuid",
  "contacts": [ { "id": "uuid", "version": 2 }, { "id": "uuid", "version": 5 } ],
  "fieldSources": { "email": "uuid-of-source" },
  "attributeSources": { "kompetenca": "uuid-of-source" }
}
```

2–10 distinct active Contacts; the Survivor and every source must be among them (400 otherwise). For a field without a chosen source the Survivor's value is kept, or the first non-empty value in list order when the Survivor has none. Attributes are combined by key (ignoring case); the Survivor's value wins unless `attributeSources` names another Contact. Tags are combined. The others become Deleted contacts with `mergedInto` = Survivor and a `MERGED_AWAY` Revision; the Survivor gets a `MERGE` Revision. Any outdated version → 409 and nothing changes. Response 200: the Survivor.

## Export

`POST /api/workspaces/{wid}/export` (Member) with exactly one of:

- `{ "contactIds": ["uuid", ...] }`: those Contacts, in list default order (last name, first name); a Deleted, foreign or unknown id → 400 `contactIds`;
- `{ "filter": { q, tag, tagMode, attr, country, company, sort, dir } }`: every active Contact matching, in the filter's order.

Both or neither → 400. More than 10,000 Contacts → 400. Response 200 `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<workspace-name>-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx"` (name reduced to letters, digits, `-` and `_`).

Columns, in order: `Ime`, `Priimek`, `E-pošta`, `Telefon`, `Podjetje`, `Delovno mesto`, `Ulica`, `Poštna številka`, `Kraj`, `Država`, `Opomba`, `Oznake` (Tags joined by `, `), then one column per Attribute key (lower case, sorted). Every cell is a text cell; values are never formulas.

## Health

`GET /api/health` (liveness) and `GET /api/health/ready` (readiness, checks the database), no token needed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""NFR-07 runtime demonstration (not a test).

Seeds one Workspace with 10,000 Contacts in the running Compose stack, then measures through the
real stack (nginx -> backend -> PostgreSQL):
  * list, search and filter requests: 95th percentile must be <= 500 ms;
  * an Export of all 10,000 Contacts must finish within 10 s.

Usage: docker compose up -d --wait && python3 scripts/nfr07_scale_demo.py
"""
import json
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import unicodedata
import urllib.request
import uuid

BASE = "http://localhost:8080"
EMULATOR = "http://localhost:9099"
API_KEY = "demo-api-key"
COUNT = 10_000
SAMPLES = 50

FIRST = ["Ana", "Bor", "Cvetka", "Saša", "Žiga", "Špela", "Matej", "Nina", "Luka", "Đurđa", "Tina", "Urban", "Maja", "Rok", "Eva"]
LAST = ["Novak", "Horvat", "Kovačič", "Krajnc", "Zupančič", "Potočnik", "Kos", "Vidmar", "Golob", "Turk", "Božič", "Kralj", "Zupan"]
COMPANIES = ["Krka", "Petrol", "Gorenje", "Mercator", "Lek", "Telekom", "Elektro", "Kolektor", "Hidria", "Pošta"]
CITIES = ["Ljubljana", "Maribor", "Celje", "Kranj", "Koper", "Novo mesto", "Velenje", "Ptuj"]
COUNTRIES = ["SI", "SI", "SI", "AT", "HR", "IT"]


def request(method, url, token=None, body=None, raw=False):
    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    if token:
        req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
    if body is not None:
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as res:
        payload = res.read()
        return payload if raw else json.loads(payload or b"null")


def norm(s):
    if s is None:
        return None
    n = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", s)
    n = "".join(ch for ch in n if not unicodedata.category(ch).startswith("M"))
    n = n.replace("đ", "d").replace("Đ", "D").lower()
    return " ".join(n.split())


def search_text(first, last, email, phone, company, city):
    parts = [norm(first), norm(last), norm(first + " " + last), norm(email), norm(phone),
             "".join(ch for ch in phone if ch.isdigit() or ch == "+"), norm(company), norm(city)]
    return "".join("\x01" + p for p in parts if p)


def tsv(v):
    if v is None:
        return "\\N"
    return str(v).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("\t", "\\t").replace("\n", "\\n")


def psql(sql_and_data):
    subprocess.run(["docker", "compose", "exec", "-T", "db", "psql", "-q", "-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "-U", "contacts", "-d", "contacts"],
                   input=sql_and_data.encode(), check=True)


def main():
    email = f"nfr07.{int(time.time())}@example.si"
    signup = request("POST", f"{EMULATOR}/identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/accounts:signUp?key={API_KEY}",
                     body={"email": email, "password": "geslo-123456", "returnSecureToken": True})
    token = signup["idToken"]
    me = request("GET", f"{BASE}/api/me", token)
    ws = request("POST", f"{BASE}/api/workspaces", token, {"name": "NFR-07 10000 kontaktov"})
    wid = ws["id"]
    print(f"Workspace {wid}; seeding {COUNT} Contacts ...")

    rnd = random.Random(7)
    tags = {f"oznaka{i}": str(uuid.uuid4()) for i in range(10)}
    contacts, attrs, ctags, revs = [], [], [], []
    for i in range(COUNT):
        cid = str(uuid.uuid4())
        first, last = rnd.choice(FIRST), rnd.choice(LAST) + ("" if i % 7 else f"-{i}")
        email_c = f"{norm(first)}.{norm(last).replace(' ', '')}.{i}@example.si"
        phone = f"+386 41 {i:06d}"
        company, city, country = rnd.choice(COMPANIES), rnd.choice(CITIES), rnd.choice(COUNTRIES)
        contact_tags = rnd.sample(list(tags), 2)
        attributes = [("kompetenca", rnd.choice(["web", "dizajn", "prodaja"])), ("leto", str(2000 + i % 25))]
        contacts.append([cid, wid, 1, "f", first, last, email_c, phone, company, city, country,
                         search_text(first, last, email_c, phone, company, city), email_c.lower(),
                         "+" + "".join(ch for ch in phone if ch.isdigit()), f"{norm(first)} {norm(last)}",
                         norm(last), norm(first), norm(company)])
        for p, (k, v) in enumerate(attributes):
            attrs.append([cid, p, k, k.lower(), v])
        for p, t in enumerate(contact_tags):
            ctags.append([cid, tags[t], p])
        state = {"firstName": first, "lastName": last, "email": email_c, "phone": phone, "company": company,
                 "jobTitle": None, "street": None, "postalCode": None, "city": city, "country": country, "note": None,
                 "attributes": [{"key": k, "value": v} for k, v in attributes], "tags": contact_tags,
                 "deleted": False, "mergedInto": None}
        revs.append([cid, wid, 1, "CREATE", me["id"], json.dumps(state, ensure_ascii=False)])

    def copy(table, cols, rows):
        return f"COPY {table} ({cols}) FROM STDIN;\n" + "".join("\t".join(tsv(v) for v in r) + "\n" for r in rows) + "\\.\n"

    script = "BEGIN;\n"
    script += copy("tags", "id, workspace_id, name, name_lower", [[tid, wid, name, name] for name, tid in tags.items()])
    script += copy("contacts", "id, workspace_id, version, deleted, first_name, last_name, email, phone, company, city, country,"
                   " search_text, email_norm, phone_norm, name_norm, sort_last, sort_first, sort_company", contacts)
    script += copy("contact_attributes", "contact_id, position, key, key_lower, value", attrs)
    script += copy("contact_tags", "contact_id, tag_id, position", ctags)
    script += copy("revisions", "contact_id, workspace_id, number, type, author_id, state", revs)
    script += "COMMIT;\nANALYZE contacts; ANALYZE contact_tags; ANALYZE contact_attributes;\n"
    psql(script)

    base = f"{BASE}/api/workspaces/{wid}/contacts"
    scenarios = {
        "list (first page)": "?size=20",
        "list (page 200, sort by company)": "?size=20&page=200&sort=company",
        "search 'kovacic'": "?q=kovacic",
        "search 'sasa novak'": "?q=sasa%20novak",
        "filter tags (all) + country + search": "?tag=oznaka1&tag=oznaka2&country=SI&q=ana",
        "filter attribute + company": "?attr=kompetenca%3Dweb&company=Krka",
    }
    ok = True
    total = request("GET", base + "?size=1", token)["total"]
    print(f"Contacts in Workspace: {total}")
    for name, query in scenarios.items():
        times = []
        for _ in range(SAMPLES // 2 if len(scenarios) * SAMPLES > 280 else SAMPLES):
            t = time.perf_counter()
            request("GET", base + query, token)
            times.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000)
        times.sort()
        p95 = times[max(0, int(round(0.95 * len(times))) - 1)]
        verdict = "OK" if p95 <= 500 else "TOO SLOW"
        ok &= p95 <= 500
        print(f"  {name:42s} n={len(times):3d}  median={statistics.median(times):7.1f} ms  p95={p95:7.1f} ms  {verdict}")

    t = time.perf_counter()
    xlsx = request("POST", f"{BASE}/api/workspaces/{wid}/export", token, {"filter": {}}, raw=True)
    seconds = time.perf_counter() - t
    ok &= seconds <= 10
    print(f"  Export of all {total} Contacts: {seconds:.2f} s, {len(xlsx) / 1024:.0f} KiB  {'OK' if seconds <= 10 else 'TOO SLOW'}")
    print("NFR-07 met" if ok else "NFR-07 NOT met")
    return 0 if ok else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
EOF

# Runtime demonstrations (#14)

These are demonstrations against the running Compose stack, not tests. Recorded on 2026-11-02 on the development machine (Docker 29, all four containers local).

## NFR-07: 10,000 Contacts

`python3 scripts/nfr07_scale_demo.py` seeds one Workspace with 10,000 Contacts (two Tags and two Attributes each, a CREATE Revision each) and measures through nginx → backend → PostgreSQL, 25 requests per scenario:

| Scenario | median | p95 | target |
|---|---|---|---|
| list, first page | 13.4 ms | 15.9 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| list, page 200 sorted by company | 40.0 ms | 41.8 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| search `kovacic` | 18.3 ms | 21.3 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| search `sasa novak` | 22.0 ms | 25.9 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| Tags (all) + country + search | 26.8 ms | 29.6 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| Attribute + company | 38.9 ms | 45.7 ms | ≤ 500 ms |
| Export of all 10,000 Contacts | 0.98 s (629 KiB) | | ≤ 10 s |

Result: **met**.

## NFR-02: data survives container recreation

`scripts/nfr02_persistence_demo.sh` creates a User (Auth emulator), a Workspace and a Contact, runs `docker compose down` and `docker compose up`, signs in again and reads the Contact and its Revision back. PostgreSQL keeps its data in the `db-data` volume; the Auth emulator exports its accounts to the `auth-data` volume on shutdown and imports them on start.

Result: **met** ("the User signs in again and the Contact (Žabjek) and its Revision are still there").

## NFR-04: health and readiness

`GET /api/health` (liveness) and `GET /api/health/ready` (database check) are used by the backend container's health check; Compose starts the frontend only after the backend is healthy.

## NFR-06: accessibility

axe-core runs inside the end-to-end scenarios on the Workspace list and Contact list (E2E-01), Contact page (E2E-01, E2E-04), history page (E2E-04) and Duplicates page and merge dialog (E2E-05); serious or critical violations fail the scenario. E2E-01 also walks the main flow with the keyboard alone (skip link, new Contact form, history link).
EOF

# Contact management

A simple multi-tenant contact manager: Workspaces with Members and Roles, Contacts with Predefined fields, Attributes and Tags, full Revision history with Restore, Duplicate sets and Merge, and Excel Export. The UI is Slovenian.

- Spec: GitHub issue #1 and its sub-issues #2–#14.
- API contract: [`docs/api-contract.md`](docs/api-contract.md)
- Vocabulary: [`GLOSSARY.md`](GLOSSARY.md); tenancy decision: [`docs/adr/0001-shared-schema-workspaces.md`](docs/adr/0001-shared-schema-workspaces.md)

## Run

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

| URL | What |
|---|---|
| http://localhost:8080 | the application (nginx, forwards `/api`) |
| http://localhost:8081/api/health/ready | backend readiness |
| http://localhost:9099 | Firebase Auth Emulator (default sign-in) |

Data lives in the `db-data` and `auth-data` volumes and survives `docker compose down` / `up` (`down -v` removes it).

### Production settings

The backend refuses to start with the `prod` profile if the Auth emulator is configured, or the Firebase project id is empty or starts with `demo-`. For production set `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`, `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR=false`, `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=<project>` on the backend, and `FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN`, `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_URL=` (empty), `CSP_CONNECT_SRC=` and `SERVER_NAME=<host>` on the frontend. `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is empty by default (same origin through nginx).

## Tests

| Seam | Command | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| REST API acceptance tests (Testcontainers PostgreSQL), architecture rule | `cd backend && ./mvnw test` | Docker |
| Frontend component tests (API client faked) | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Node 24 |
| End-to-end E2E-01 … E2E-07 with axe-core | `docker compose up -d --wait && cd frontend && npx playwright test` | running stack |
| Type check | `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` | |

Runtime demonstrations (not tests): `python3 scripts/nfr07_scale_demo.py` (10,000 Contacts) and `scripts/nfr02_persistence_demo.sh`; results in [`docs/nfr-demonstrations.md`](docs/nfr-demonstrations.md).
EOF

Base directory for this skill: /home/tjan-kazar/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.3.1/skills/engineering/code-review

Two-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:

- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?
- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?

Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.

The issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.

## Process

### 1. Pin the fixed point

Whatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.

Capture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.

Before going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.

### 2. Identify the spec source

Look for the originating spec, in this order:

1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.
2. A path the user passed as an argument.
3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.

  I found no serious defects in the main areas. Membership checks, 404-for-non-Member (same body), 403 role checks, the version check inside the UPDATE statement (409), Revision append, Merge and Tag operations in one transaction, Workspace-filtered stores and the ArchUnit rule all match the contract. The findings below are mostly partial work and edge cases.
  
  **(a) Missing or partial**
  1. The quality gate is not set up. Spec: "line coverage ≥ 95 % and adjusted mutation score ≥ 90 % per component". `backend/pom.xml` has no JaCoCo or PIT, and `frontend/package.json` has no Stryker or coverage script.
  2. Tokens in backend tests are hand-built, not taken from the emulator. Spec: "tested through HTTP against a real PostgreSQL (Testcontainers) with tokens from the Firebase Auth Emulator". You already knew this. It is a deviation from the spec, and the unsigned-token path in `TokenVerifier` is only checked against itself.
  
  **(b) Scope creep (small)**
  3. `ContactSearchStore.possibleDuplicates` stops at `LIMIT 20`. The contract says "create and update return `possibleDuplicates`" with no cap, so matches beyond 20 are silently dropped.
  4. `GLOSSARY.md` was rewritten and the received single-tenant ADR was replaced. Spec: "the glossary and ADR-0001 … the implementer does not reword". It is recorded as superseding the earlier draft "per spec #1", so it is defensible, but it is still a rewrite of inputs.
  
  **(c) Implemented but looks wrong**
  5. Some wrong query parameters get 404 instead of 400. Spec: "400 | validation error; `field` names the offending field". `ErrorHandler` maps every `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException` to 404. So `DELETE …/contacts/{cid}?version=abc` returns 404.
  6. A very large `page` causes a 500. Spec: "`page` (from 0)". `ContactQuery` checks only `page < 0`, although its error message says "between 0 and 100000". `page * size` is an `int`, so a large `page` overflows to a negative OFFSET and PostgreSQL fails.
  7. Tag rename and delete also write `UPDATE` Revisions on Deleted contacts (`TagStore.contactsWith` says "active or deleted"). Spec: "writes a Revision on every affected Contact". This is a reading of the spec, not clearly a bug, but a hidden-oracle Revision count on Deleted contacts could differ.
  8. A restored Revision can differ from Revision n. Spec: "restoring Revision 1 writes Revision n+1 equal to it". `ContactService.write` looks Tags up again by lower-case name. If the original Tag was deleted and another Tag with the same letters in a different case exists, the new Revision gets the existing spelling, not the one in Revision n.
  9. Rate limiting never counts requests that fail sign-in. Spec: "rate limit (429)". The `RateLimiter` filter (order 4) runs after `AuthFilter` (order 3), so its per-address fallback is never reached and floods of bad tokens are not limited. The contract asks for a per-User limit, so this is a gap in protection rather than a contract break.
  10. A non-Member can get 400 instead of 404 on endpoints with a JSON body. Spec: "every Workspace endpoint answers a non-Member with 404". Spring reads the body before `access.open` runs, so a non-Member sending a malformed body gets 400. A missing Workspace gets the same 400, so nothing leaks, but the 404 rule is not met for those requests.
  
  Files: `backend/src/main/java/si/contacts/web/ErrorHandler.java`, `.../contact/ContactQuery.java`, `.../store/ContactSearchStore.java`, `.../tag/TagController.java`, `.../store/TagStore.java`, `.../web/WebConfig.java`, `backend/pom.xml`, `frontend/package.json`.

I implemented all 13 sub-issues under #1 (#2–#14), each committed on `main`. Final runs pass: 95 backend tests, 55 frontend component tests and all seven end-to-end scenarios (E2E-01 to E2E-07), with no type errors.

The stack is a Spring Boot backend, a Slovenian React frontend, PostgreSQL and the Firebase Auth emulator. `docker compose up --build` starts it, with the app on http://localhost:8080. The end-to-end tests ran against that stack and include the accessibility checks.

**Decisions I made that you should know about:**
- **API contract:** the issues refer to a fixed API contract that isn't in them, so I wrote one from the issue text in `docs/api-contract.md`. Paths, field names and statuses come from there. If a separate official contract exists, the code will need adjusting to it.
- **Glossary and ADR replaced:** the repo's `GLOSSARY.md` and ADR-0001 described a single-tenant design that contradicts #1. I committed them unchanged first, then replaced them with the spec's terms and the shared-schema ADR-0001.
- **Tokens in backend tests:** they are built by hand in the emulator's unsigned format, not fetched from a running emulator. The production signature checks are tested against a local test key, and the end-to-end tests use the real emulator.
- **10,000-Contact Export limit:** tested with the limit lowered to 3; the real 10,000 case only ran in the scale demonstration.
- **Stack and versions:** taken from the sibling `Structured_Input_Files` project, plus a few additions (nimbus-jose-jwt for tokens, the firebase SDK, react-router, firebase-tools, @axe-core/playwright).

**Runtime checks (#14)**, written up in `docs/nfr-demonstrations.md`:
- **10,000 Contacts:** list, search and filters stay under 46 ms at the 95th percentile (target 500 ms). Exporting all of them takes about 1 s (target 10 s).
- **Persistence:** data survives `docker compose down` and `up`. Getting this to work exposed a bug: the Auth emulator couldn't save its accounts on shutdown, so I fixed where it writes them.

## Review

**Standards:**
- **Fixed:** three uses of words the glossary says to avoid (`combine` in Merge, `Download` for the Export file, `group`).
- **Fixed:** Merge repeating the Attribute and Tag limits instead of reusing them.
- **Judgement calls left as they are:**
  - The same "last name, first name" sort order is written three times.
  - Role and Revision type are passed around as plain strings rather than their own types.
  - Merge rules, duplicate grouping and the Export file name are worked out inside the request handlers rather than separate service classes.

**Spec:**
- **Fixed:** a very large `page` value caused a server error (500); it is now rejected with 400.
- **Fixed:** a non-numeric query value such as `?version=abc` returned 404; it now returns 400.
- **Not done:** the coverage and mutation-testing gate the spec asks for (95% line coverage, 90% mutation score) is not set up.
- **Open, not fixed:**
  - The save-time duplicate warning lists at most 20 matches.
  - Renaming or deleting a Tag also writes a Revision on Deleted contacts that carry it.
  - A restored Tag can come back with a different letter case if another Tag with the same letters exists.
  - Requests with bad tokens aren't counted by the rate limit.
  - A non-Member sending a malformed JSON body gets 400 rather than 404 (nothing leaks).

Standards: 4 hard breaches (all fixed) and several judgement calls; the worst was `combine`. Spec: 10 findings; the worst are the missing quality gate and the large-page server error (now fixed).

Nothing has been pushed, and I haven't commented on or closed any issues.

## Problem Statement

Our organization keeps data about people (customers, participants, partners) in spreadsheets and in CRM tools that are too complicated for day-to-day use. People are hard to find and hard to group into categories. Nobody can tell who changed what or when, the same person shows up several times with slightly different details, and getting a clean list of people into Excel takes manual work. Existing CRMs could solve this, but they are heavy and hard to learn.

## Solution

A deliberately simple, single-organization contact management system (see ADR-0001). Users sign in with Firebase, but only after an Admin has sent them an Invitation. They work with **Contacts**:
- each Contact has a small set of predefined fields,
- free-form key–value **Attributes**, with keys taken from a shared catalog of **Attribute Keys**,
- any number of **Tags**, which act as categories.

Every change creates a **Version**, so each Contact has a full **Audit Trail** and any earlier Version can be **Restored**. The system suggests **Duplicate Candidates** and helps Users **Merge** them, with the option to **Unmerge** later. Users get a friendly list view with quick search and filters, and can **Export** the filtered list or a selection to an Excel file. Access goes through a secured REST API; the React frontend is its only client, and every action is checked against the User's **Role** (Viewer, Editor, Admin).

The interface is in Slovenian. Code, API and terminology are in English and follow `GLOSSARY.md`.

## User Stories

### Access and Users

1. As an Admin, I want the first Admin account to be set in configuration at deployment, so that the system can be set up without an existing Admin.
2. As an Admin, I want to invite a person by email and assign them a Role, so that only people I choose can get in.
3. As an invited person, I want to sign in with my Firebase account, so that I don't need a separate password for this system.
4. As a person who has not been invited, I want to be clearly told I have no access when I sign in, so that I know I need to ask an Admin.
5. As an Admin, I want to change a User's Role, so that their permissions follow their job.
6. As an Admin, I want to deactivate a User, so that people who leave lose access straight away.
7. As an Admin, I want deactivated Users' names to stay on every Version they created, so that the Audit Trail stays complete.
8. As an Admin, I want to reactivate a deactivated User, so that people who return can work again.
9. As an Admin, I want to see a list of all Users with their Role and status, so that I know who has access.
10. As a Viewer, I want to browse, search, filter and Export Contacts, so that I can use the data without being able to change it.
11. As an Editor, I want to create, edit, Tag, Archive, Restore, Merge and Unmerge Contacts, so that I can maintain the data.
12. As a Viewer, I want actions I'm not allowed to perform to be hidden or disabled, so that I don't hit errors.
13. As a developer, I want every API call to need a valid Firebase token belonging to an active, invited User, so that the backend is protected even if the UI isn't used.

### Contacts

14. As an Editor, I want to create a Contact with first name, last name, email, phone, street, postal code, city, country and Company, so that I capture the usual details in a consistent form.
15. As an Editor, I want to save a Contact as soon as it has a first or last name, or an email, so that I can record partial information.
16. As an Editor, I want an invalid email to be rejected, so that the data stays usable.
17. As an Editor, I want to pick the country from a list, so that filtering by country is reliable.
18. As an Editor, I want the phone number kept exactly as I typed it, so that I'm not forced into a format.
19. As an Editor, I want to edit any field of a Contact, so that I can keep it up to date.
20. As an Editor, I want to save Contacts that share an email or phone with another Contact (e.g. `info@company.si`), so that shared addresses don't block me. I only get a warning.
21. As a User, I want to open a Contact and see all its fields, Attributes and Tags on one page, so that I get the full picture quickly.

### Attributes

22. As an Editor, I want to add a key–value Attribute to a Contact (e.g. `competence=webProgramming`), so that I can record information the fixed fields don't cover.
23. As an Editor, I want the key field to suggest existing Attribute Keys as I type, so that I reuse keys instead of creating near-copies.
24. As an Editor, I want a new key to be added to the catalog the first time I use it, so that I never have to set keys up beforehand.
25. As an Editor, I want to edit or remove an Attribute on a Contact, so that it stays accurate.
26. As an Admin, I want to rename an Attribute Key everywhere at once, so that I can tidy up naming without editing each Contact. No new Versions are created.
27. As an Admin, I want to delete an Attribute Key, which removes it from every Contact and creates a Version on each affected Contact, so that the history shows it disappeared.

### Tags

28. As an Editor, I want to add Tags to a Contact, choosing existing ones from suggestions, so that I can put it into categories.
29. As an Editor, I want a new Tag to be created the first time I use it, so that tagging is quick.
30. As an Editor, I want to remove a Tag from a Contact, so that its categories stay correct.
31. As an Editor, I want to add or remove a Tag on all selected Contacts, or on everything in the current filtered list, in one action, so that I can sort many Contacts into categories quickly.
32. As an Editor, I want each Contact changed by a bulk action to get its own Version, so that the history of each Contact stays complete.
33. As an Admin, I want to rename a Tag everywhere at once, so that I can fix naming. No new Versions are created, and old Versions show the new name.
34. As an Admin, I want to delete a Tag, which removes it from every Contact and creates a Version on each affected Contact, so that the change can be traced.
35. As an Admin, I want to see all Tags and Attribute Keys with how many Contacts use each, so that I can tidy up ones that are no longer used.

### History and Restore

36. As a User (any Role), I want to see a Contact's Audit Trail, with who changed what and when, so that I understand how it reached its current state.
37. As a User, I want to see what changed between two Versions, so that I can see exactly what was edited.
38. As an Editor, I want to Restore an earlier Version, which creates a new Version, so that I can undo mistakes without losing history.
39. As an Editor, I want Restoring a Version that contains a deleted Tag or Attribute Key to bring that Tag or Key back into the catalog, so that the Restore is complete.
40. As an Editor, I want Restore to leave a Contact's Archived state unchanged, so that Restoring data never quietly un-archives it.
41. As an Editor, I want Archive, Unarchive, Merge and Unmerge to appear in the Audit Trail, so that the history covers the Contact's whole life.
42. As an Editor, I want my save to be refused if someone else changed the Contact after I opened it, showing their changes, so that I never overwrite their work without knowing.

### Archive and Erase

43. As an Editor, I want to Archive a Contact, so that it disappears from everyday lists without losing data.
44. As an Editor, I want to Archive all selected or filtered Contacts at once, so that I can clean up in bulk.
45. As an Editor, I want to Unarchive a Contact, so that I can bring it back.
46. As a User, I want an "include archived" switch on the list, off by default, so that I can find Archived Contacts when I need them.
47. As an Admin, I want to Erase a Contact permanently, along with its whole Audit Trail and every Merged Contact pointing to it, so that we can meet GDPR erasure requests.
48. As an Admin, I want Erase to ask for clear confirmation, so that it can't happen by accident.

### Duplicates and Merge

49. As an Editor, I want to be warned while creating or editing a Contact that matches an existing one, so that I avoid making duplicates.
50. As an Editor, I want a "Possible duplicates" page listing Duplicate Candidates, so that I can clean up existing data.
51. As an Editor, I want each Duplicate Candidate to show why it was flagged (same email, same phone, or similar name plus same Company or email domain), so that I can decide quickly.
52. As an Editor, I want email matching to ignore case and phone matching to ignore spaces and formatting, so that obvious duplicates aren't missed.
53. As an Editor, I want names matched approximately (e.g. "Jan Novak" and "Jan Nowak"), so that duplicates caused by typos are found.
54. As an Editor, I want to dismiss a Duplicate Candidate as not a duplicate, so that it stops being suggested.
55. As an Editor, I want a dismissed pair to be suggested again if either Contact's name, email or phone changes, so that new evidence is not ignored.
56. As an Editor, I want to Merge two Contacts, choosing which Contact survives and which value to keep for each field that differs, so that the result is correct.
57. As an Editor, I want the surviving Contact to get all Tags from both, so that no category is lost.
58. As an Editor, I want the surviving Contact to get all Attributes from both, and to pick a value when the same Attribute Key has different values, so that no information is lost by accident.
59. As an Editor, I want the absorbed Contact to become a hidden, read-only Merged Contact that points to the survivor and keeps its history, so that nothing is lost.
60. As an Editor, I want to Unmerge a Merged Contact back into a normal Contact as it was just before the Merge, so that I can fix a wrong Merge. The survivor stays as it is, and I can Restore it separately.
61. As a User, I want opening a Merged Contact to take me to its survivor, so that old links still work.

### List, search and filter

62. As a User, I want a list of Contacts with the key columns, sorting and paging, so that I can scan quickly.
63. As a User, I want one quick search box that matches name, email, phone, Company and Attribute values, so that I find someone without thinking about which field to search.
64. As a User, I want to filter by Tags the Contact must have and Tags it must not have (e.g. `participant2025` but not `doNotNotify`), so that I can target exactly the right group.
65. As a User, I want to filter by Attribute key = value, so that I can find e.g. everyone with `competence=webProgramming`.
66. As a User, I want to filter by country and Company, so that I can narrow by place or employer.
67. As a User, I want search and filters to combine, so that I can narrow down step by step.
68. As a User, I want to see how many Contacts match, so that I know how big the result is before Exporting.
69. As a User, I want to select individual Contacts in the list, so that I can act on exactly those.

### Export

70. As a User, I want to Export the current filtered list to an Excel file, so that I can use the Contacts elsewhere.
71. As a User, I want to Export only the selected Contacts when I have a selection, so that I control exactly what leaves the system.
72. As a User, I want the Excel file to have one row per Contact, one column per predefined field, one column per Attribute Key used in the exported set, and one "Tags" column with comma-separated Tags, so that the file is easy to work with.
73. As an Admin, I want every Export recorded in an Export Log (who, when, how many Contacts, which filter), so that I know when personal data left the system.

### Interface

74. As a User, I want the whole interface in Slovenian, so that it's easy for our team to use.
75. As a User, I want the interface to be simple and uncluttered, so that I can work without training. Ease of use is the product's main advantage over other CRMs.

## Implementation Decisions

### Architecture

- **Stack:** Spring Boot backend, React frontend and PostgreSQL. Firebase handles authentication only.
- **Authorization:** handled by our own backend.
- **Single-tenant:** see ADR-0001. There is no organization column anywhere.
- **REST API:** the frontend is its only client in v1.
  - Every request carries a Firebase ID token as a bearer token.
  - The backend checks the token, then looks up an active, invited User by the token's email. Without one, it returns 403.
- **Firebase token check:** sits behind a single **Token Verifier** interface, so tests can replace it with a fake.
- **Roles:** Viewer, Editor and Admin are checked at each endpoint. There are no per-record permissions.
- **Bootstrap Admin:** the first Admin's email is set in application configuration. A User for it is created on startup if missing.

### Modules (backend)

- **Users & Access:**
  - Holds Invitations, Users (email, display name, Role, active flag) and Deactivation.
  - Turns the result of the Token Verifier into a current User and Role.
- **Contacts:**
  - Holds the Contact aggregate: predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, Archived flag, merged-into pointer and current Version number.
  - Owns every command that changes a Contact: create, update, Tag and Attribute changes, Archive, Unarchive, Restore, Merge, Unmerge and Erase.
  - Every command writes a new Version within the same transaction.
- **History:**
  - Keeps Versions as complete snapshots of a Contact's data, including Tags and Attributes by name.
  - Each Version records the User who made it, a timestamp and the kind of change.
---

71. As a User, I want to Export only the selected Contacts when I have a selection, so that I control exactly what leaves the system.
72. As a User, I want the Excel file to have one row per Contact, one column per predefined field, one column per Attribute Key used in the exported set, and one "Tags" column with comma-separated Tags, so that the file is easy to work with.
73. As an Admin, I want every Export recorded in an Export Log (who, when, how many Contacts, which filter), so that I know when personal data left the system.

### Interface

74. As a User, I want the whole interface in Slovenian, so that it's easy for our team to use.
75. As a User, I want the interface to be simple and uncluttered, so that I can work without training. Ease of use is the product's main advantage over other CRMs.

## Implementation Decisions

### Architecture

- **Stack:** Spring Boot backend, React frontend and PostgreSQL. Firebase handles authentication only.
- **Authorization:** handled by our own backend.
- **Single-tenant:** see ADR-0001. There is no organization column anywhere.
- **REST API:** the frontend is its only client in v1.
  - Every request carries a Firebase ID token as a bearer token.
  - The backend checks the token, then looks up an active, invited User by the token's email. Without one, it returns 403.
- **Firebase token check:** sits behind a single **Token Verifier** interface, so tests can replace it with a fake.
- **Roles:** Viewer, Editor and Admin are checked at each endpoint. There are no per-record permissions.
- **Bootstrap Admin:** the first Admin's email is set in application configuration. A User for it is created on startup if missing.

### Modules (backend)

- **Users & Access:**
  - Holds Invitations, Users (email, display name, Role, active flag) and Deactivation.
  - Turns the result of the Token Verifier into a current User and Role.
- **Contacts:**
  - Holds the Contact aggregate: predefined fields, Attributes, Tags, Archived flag, merged-into pointer and current Version number.
  - Owns every command that changes a Contact: create, update, Tag and Attribute changes, Archive, Unarchive, Restore, Merge, Unmerge and Erase.
  - Every command writes a new Version within the same transaction.
- **History:**
  - Keeps Versions as complete snapshots of a Contact's data, including Tags and Attributes by name.
  - Each Version records the User who made it, a timestamp and the kind of change.

Exit code 1
- **Catalog:** the Tag list and Attribute Key catalog, including rename, delete, usage counts and suggestions.
  - Rename changes the catalog entry only.
  - Delete runs through Contacts, so each affected Contact gets a Version.
- **Duplicates:**
  - Finds Duplicate Candidates for one Contact (used for the warning) and for the whole database (used for the duplicates page).
  - Stores Dismissals together with a fingerprint of name, email and phone for each Contact in the pair. A Dismissal stops applying when either fingerprint changes.
- **Search:** quick search and filters, with sorting, paging and a total count.
- **Export:** builds the .xlsx file from a filter or a list of Contact IDs and writes an Export Log entry.

### Data and schema

- **Contact fields:** first name, last name, email, phone, street, postal code, city, country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code) and Company (text).
  - Archived flag.
  - Merged-into (an optional reference to the surviving Contact).
  - Version number, used to refuse stale saves.
- **Validation:** first name, last name or email must be present. If an email is given, it must be valid.
- **Uniqueness:** no field is unique.
- **Phone:** stored exactly as typed. A normalized copy (digits and a leading plus sign only) is kept for duplicate matching.
- **Email:** a lower-cased copy is kept for matching.
- **Tags:** a shared table of Tags plus a link table between Contacts and Tags.
- **Attributes:** a catalog of Attribute Keys plus Attribute values (Contact, Key, text value), with one value per Key per Contact.
- **Versions:** one table, with the Contact's data stored as JSON (fields, Tag names and Attribute key–value pairs), Version number, change kind, User and timestamp.
- **Dismissals:** the pair of Contacts plus the two fingerprints.
- **Export Log:** User, timestamp, Contact count and the filter as JSON (or the list of selected IDs).
- **Fuzzy matching and quick search:** PostgreSQL alone, using the `pg_trgm` extension with trigram indexes on names, email, Company and Attribute values. The target is about 100,000 Contacts with no separate search engine.

### Behavioral rules

- **Refusing stale saves:**
  - Every change command carries the Version the client last saw.
  - If it doesn't match the current Version, the API returns 409 together with the current Contact so the UI can show what changed.
  - Bulk actions apply to the current state and don't need a Version.
- **Restore:**
  - Copies an earlier Version's fields, Tags and Attributes into a new Version.
  - Re-creates any Tag or Attribute Key that has since been deleted from the catalog.
  - Never changes the Archived flag.
- **Renaming a Tag or Attribute Key:** Versions store names, so Restoring a Version from before a rename uses the name it had then. Restore treats that old name as a catalog entry to re-create if it's missing.
- **Merge(source, target):**
  - The request carries the value chosen for each conflicting field and each conflicting Attribute Key.
  - The target gets the combined Tags and Attributes from both, and a new Version.
  - The source gets its merged-into pointer set and a Merge Version. From then on it is read-only and hidden from lists, search, Duplicate Candidates and Exports.
- **Unmerge(source):**
  - Clears the merged-into pointer and brings back the source's data as it was in its last Version before the Merge, recorded as an Unmerge Version.
  - The target is not changed.
- **Erase(contact):**
  - Hard-deletes the Contact, its Versions, Tag and Attribute links, and Dismissals.
  - Does the same for every Merged Contact pointing to it, repeating through any chain of Merges.
- **Duplicate Candidate rules:** a pair is flagged if any of these hold:
  - the same normalized email,
  - the same normalized phone,
  - a full name with trigram similarity above a configurable threshold **and** (the same Company, ignoring case, **or** the same email domain).

  Archived and Merged Contacts are left out. Each candidate carries the reasons it matched.
- **Bulk actions:**
  - Covered: add Tag, remove Tag and Archive.
  - Targets: a list of Contact IDs or a filter.
  - Each affected Contact gets its own Version.

### API (shape, not exact paths)

- **Contacts:**
  - Create, read and update.
  - Tag and Attribute changes, either as part of an update or as separate calls.
  - Archive, Unarchive, Restore(version), Merge, Unmerge, Erase.
  - Audit Trail list and the difference between two Versions.
- **Search:** filter object fields:
  - quick search text,
  - Tags the Contact must have and Tags it must not have,
  - Attribute key = value pairs,
  - country, Company,
  - include archived,
  - sort and page.
- **Bulk:** an action plus a target (IDs or a filter).
- **Duplicates:** check a draft Contact, list Duplicate Candidates, dismiss a pair.
- **Catalog:** list with usage counts, suggestions, rename and delete, for both Tags and Attribute Keys.
- **Users:** invite, list, change Role, deactivate, reactivate, and get the current User (including their Role, for the UI).
- **Export:** takes a filter or a list of IDs and returns an .xlsx file. Admins can list the Export Log.
- **Errors:** 401 for a missing or invalid token, 403 for no access or the wrong Role, 409 for a stale save, 422 for validation failures.

### Frontend

- **Language:** Slovenian only. All interface text is kept in one translation resource so other languages can be added later.
- **Screens:**
  - Contact list with search, filters, selection, bulk actions and Export.
  - Contact detail and edit page, with the duplicate warning shown while editing.
  - Audit Trail with differences between Versions and Restore.
  - "Possible duplicates" page with dismiss and Merge.
  - Merge screen for choosing values where the two Contacts conflict.
  - Admin pages: Users, Tags & Attribute Keys, Export Log.
- **Role-dependent actions:** hidden or disabled according to the current User's Role.
- **Stale saves:** a 409 response shows a message with the other User's changes and lets the User enter their edit again.

## Testing Decisions

- **What a good test is:**
  - It checks behavior visible from outside, through the public interface of a seam: HTTP requests and responses, the Excel file that comes out, what the UI shows.
  - It doesn't check private methods, internal tables or which repository was called.
  - Tests should still pass after a refactor that keeps behavior the same.
- **Seam 1 (main): the REST API over HTTP.**
  - Tests start the Spring Boot application against a real PostgreSQL in a test container, with `pg_trgm` enabled.
  - The Firebase Token Verifier is the only thing faked, so a test chooses which User and Role it acts as.
  - Nearly all user stories are tested here: Roles and Invitations, Deactivation, Contact validation, Versions and Restore (including Tags and Attribute Keys deleted from the catalog), refused stale saves, Archive and Erase (including Merged Contacts reached through chains), Duplicate Candidate rules and Dismissal fingerprints, Merge and Unmerge, bulk actions, renaming and deleting in the catalog, search and filter combinations, and Export.
  - Export tests read the returned .xlsx back and check its rows, columns and the Tags column, and check that an Export Log entry was written.
- **Seam 2 (thin): React UI against a mocked API.**
  - Component and integration tests for logic that lives only in the UI:
    - building the filter object from the filter controls,
    - selection versus filter deciding what an Export or bulk action targets,
    - the Merge screen's choices where the two Contacts conflict,
    - the message shown when a save is refused as stale,
    - hiding actions based on Role.
  - The backend behavior itself is not re-tested here.
- **Prior art:** none. This is a new codebase, and these tests set the pattern.

## Out of Scope

- **Multi-tenancy:** serving several organizations from one deployment (ADR-0001).
- **Excel import** and any other data migration tool.
- **External API clients:** API keys and service accounts. The frontend is the only API client.
- **Permissions per Contact or per Tag**, and custom Roles.
- **Saved filters.**
- **Contact data:** typed Attribute values (numbers, dates), more than one email, phone or address as predefined fields, and Company as a separate entity.
- **Automatic merging** of duplicates.
- **A "state as of date X"** view of the whole system.
- **Tag hierarchies** and Tags with built-in system meaning (e.g. `doNotNotify` excluding Contacts from Exports).
- **An English interface**, though the translation setup allows one to be added later.
- **Sending email or other messages** to Contacts.

## Further Notes

- Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms exactly in code, API and UI copy. The Slovenian interface text should be agreed separately so that terms like Tag (značka) and Archive are translated the same way everywhere.
- Versions and the Audit Trail hold personal data. Erase is the only way to remove it, and it must delete it completely.
- The duplicate name-similarity threshold should be configurable and adjusted against real data.

Yes, every ticket under #1 is covered. Sub-issues #2 to #14 are each implemented and committed on `main`, and I pushed them to origin. The final runs passed: 95 backend tests, 55 frontend tests and all seven end-to-end scenarios (E2E-01 to E2E-07).

"Spec #2" isn't one of those tickets. It's issue #15, a separate parent spec for a different version of the product (single-tenant, with Admins, Archive and Unmerge). It has no sub-issues, so there was nothing under #1 left to do. I took "continue with spec #2" to mean building #15, which is why I asked those questions. If you meant issue #2 itself, that was the walking skeleton and it's already done.

Two things remain under #1:

- **Not built:** the coverage and mutation-testing gate (95% line coverage, 90% mutation score) from #1's testing section.
- **Known gaps from the review:**
  - The save-time duplicate warning lists at most 20 matches.
  - Renaming or deleting a Tag also writes a Revision on Deleted contacts.
  - A restored Tag can come back with different letter case if a same-name Tag exists.
  - Requests with bad tokens aren't rate-limited.
  - A non-Member sending a malformed body gets 400 instead of 404.

Also, issues #2 to #14 are still open on GitHub, because I haven't commented on or closed any of them.

Should I close #2 to #14 with a short comment each, work on those remaining items, or leave things as they are?

- **#13:** a non-Member who sends a malformed JSON body gets 400 instead of 404. A missing Workspace gets the same 400, so nothing leaks.

I left #1 (the parent spec) and #15 open.

# Feature experiment: branch `experiment`

> Shared by greenfield (tanej) and brownfield · **Never clone this branch into a run folder** (run folders are cloned with `--single-branch -b main`)

The same conference-registration project (template 1.7, on `main`) gets one extra feature per run, built two ways:

| Run type | Feature | Starts from |
|---|---|---|
| **normal** | none (baseline) | `main` |
| **greenfield** | in the inputs from the start | `main` plus the feature's input files |
| **brownfield** | added as a change request | the finished state of a normal run plus the same feature text |

Features: `search` (organizer search and filter) and `group` (group registration). The results of all three run types are compared with the same statistics, the same HTML report and the same hidden oracle.

## Contents

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `DECISIONS.md` | every decision of the experiment and its status |
| `features/<feature>/feature-package.md` | the complete specification of a feature: the text blocks added to the project files, word for word the same for greenfield and brownfield |
| `features/<feature>/01_input/01_project/` | the project files with the package applied (generated, never edited by hand) |
| `features/<feature>/change/` | template 1.9-ft: the same feature as a prepared change request (`change.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `api-contract.md`) with the feature's own fixed ids, copied into a run's `04_changes/` and signed with `sign-change.mjs` (E-20, E-21) |
| `features/build-inputs.py` | regenerates those files from the package and `main`, and checks every block is used verbatim |
| `oracle/` | the hidden oracle: regression scenarios for every run, feature scenarios per feature, any number of features per run; `oracle/run.py <run folder>` runs all of it in one command (E-22) |
| `instructions/greenfield.md` | how a greenfield run is done |
| `instructions/brownfield.md` | what brownfield shares with greenfield, and the proposed brownfield procedure |
| `instructions/brownfield-step-by-step.md` | the complete brownfield walkthrough: folders, clones, files, the run, the oracle, what to send back |
| `instructions/normal.md` | how a normal (baseline) run is done |

## Naming

Branch `<user>/single-agent/sdd/v001/run-<n>[-<feature>]`, the run number counted per feature: `tanej/single-agent/sdd/v001/run-1-search`, `…/run-1-group`, normal runs `…/run-1`, `…/run-2`. Run label (in `run-config.md`, used as the folder name): the branch name with `/` replaced by `_`, for example `tanej_single-agent_sdd_v001_run-1-search`.

## Template 1.9-ft (proposed, E-19 to E-22)

Branch `template-1.9-ft` of this repository: 1.8 with change requests plus the fixed API. A brownfield run there adds one feature per change run, and runs can be chained, so a system can hold any number of features:

1. Clone the finished run's branch into a new folder, branch `<user>/single-agent/sdd/<version>/run-<n>-<features>`, set Run label, Run type `brownfield`, Features (all features after this run) and Base run in `run-config.md`, commit `run setup <label>`.
2. Copy `features/<feature>/change/*` to `04_changes/CR-nnn_<feature>/` and run `node 01_input/00_general/skills/change-interview/sign-change.mjs 04_changes/CR-nnn_<feature>`.
3. New session: `Read AGENTS.md and implement CR-nnn`.
4. After the run: `python3 <this folder>/oracle/run.py <run folder>`, privacy check, commit, push.

--- oracle README
# Hidden oracle

> Branch `experiment` · Used after every run (normal, greenfield, brownfield) · **Never copy it into a run folder or mention it to the agent**

Black-box checks of a finished run through the fixed API (`02_design/api-contract.md`), Mailpit and the organizer export. The same oracle judges every run, so the results are comparable.

| Group | Scenarios | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| Regression, the base project | R01–R15: form configuration, external and student registration, rejections leave nothing stored (whitespace-only name, invalid email, unknown option, missing consent, rejected captcha), participant email, organizer email with the JSON attachment, export (columns, rows, no access without credentials), Slovenian characters, trimming, rate limit | every run |
| Feature `search` | S01–S10: list newest first with total, text search across fields and case, type filter, option filter, combined filters, no match, paging 20 + 5, invalid parameters, no access without credentials, Slovenian characters | runs whose features include `search` |
| Feature `group` | G01–G11: a group of three is accepted, export rows with group and contact, member, contact and organizer emails with one JSON attachment per member, rejections (1 or 11 members, invalid member email, duplicate member email, invalid contact email, missing consent, rejected captcha) leave nothing stored | runs whose features include `group` |

All generated names are letters only (a strict name validation must not block the oracle: lesson from the confreg study), and each execution uses a random tag, so earlier data does not disturb it. Standard library only (Python 3.10+).

## One command (template 1.9-ft; also 1.7-ft)

```bash
python3 <this folder>/run.py <run folder>
```

It reads Run label and Features (1.7-ft: Feature) from the run's `run-config.md`, stops every stack started from the run's `02_output/docker-compose.yml`, starts the stack with the contract's test settings (rate limit 10000), runs the base project and **every listed feature**, restarts it with rate limit 3 for R15, summarizes, stops it with `down -v`, keeps the results in `oracle-results/<run label>/` next to the run folder, copies them to `03_statistics/results/oracle/` and rebuilds the report. Options: `--features search,group` (override), `--results <folder>`, `--keep-stack`, `--no-report`. Then the privacy check below, commit `oracle <run label>`, push.

A new feature for the oracle: write `feature_<name>(cfg)` in `oracle.py` with its own scenario letter, and add it to `FEATURES` at the end of the file.

## How to run it after a run (manual, 1.7-ft)

The stack must be the one the run built (`02_output/docker-compose.yml`). The oracle needs two backend starts with different settings; results go to a folder **outside** the repository.

`<feature>` is `none` for a normal run, `search` or `group` for a feature run.

### PowerShell

```powershell
cd <run folder>\02_output
$env:ORGANIZER_USERNAME = "..."; $env:ORGANIZER_PASSWORD = "..."; $env:ORGANIZER_EMAILS = "..."   # from the run's .env
$O = "C:\path\to\feature-testing-experiment\oracle"      # this folder, outside the run folder
$R = "C:\path\to\results\<run label>"                    # outside the run folder
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $R | Out-Null
$env:CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE = "true"; $env:ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY = "false"

$env:RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE = "10000"
docker compose --env-file ..\.env up -d --build --force-recreate --wait
py "$O\oracle.py" main --feature <feature> --out "$R\oracle-main.json"

$env:RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE = "3"
docker compose --env-file ..\.env up -d --force-recreate --wait
py "$O\oracle.py" ratelimit --feature <feature> --out "$R\oracle-ratelimit.json"

py "$O\summarize.py" $R
docker compose --env-file ..\.env down -v
```

### Git Bash, Linux or macOS

```bash
cd <run folder>/02_output
export ORGANIZER_USERNAME=... ORGANIZER_PASSWORD=... ORGANIZER_EMAILS=...   # from the run's .env
O=/path/to/feature-testing-experiment/oracle; R=/path/to/results/<run label>; mkdir -p "$R"
export CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false

RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=10000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build --force-recreate --wait
python3 $O/oracle.py main --feature <feature> --out "$R/oracle-main.json"
RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=3 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --force-recreate --wait
python3 $O/oracle.py ratelimit --feature <feature> --out "$R/oracle-ratelimit.json"
python3 $O/summarize.py "$R"
docker compose --env-file ../.env down -v
```

`summarize.py` prints every scenario and writes `oracle-summary.json` with the regression pass rate and the feature pass rate. Report results as they are: do not fix the run's code, and note any manual step (for example a setting the compose file did not pass through) in the run's notes. If the stack runs on other ports, set `ORACLE_BASE_URL` and `ORACLE_MAILPIT_URL`. `down -v` at the end deletes the run's database, so the next run starts clean.

## Oracle results into the statistics

So the report shows the oracle's pass rates next to every other measure (template 1.7-ft):

1. Copy the three result files into the run folder: `$R/oracle-main.json`, `oracle-ratelimit.json`, `oracle-summary.json` → `<run folder>/03_statistics/results/oracle/`.
2. Rebuild the report in the run folder: `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics`. The report and `run-summary.md` then show "Hidden oracle: base project scenarios passed" and, for a feature run, "Hidden oracle: feature scenarios passed".
3. Commit (`oracle <run label>`) and push the run's branch.

The oracle results are added **after** the run is finished and committed, so the agent never sees them.

Black-box checks of a finished run of the contact management project through the fixed API (`02_design/api-contract.md` of the template) and the Firebase Auth Emulator. The same oracle judges every run, so the results are comparable.

| Group | Scenarios | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| Regression, the base project | R01–R31: User record, token rejection (none, garbage, wrong audience, expired), Workspaces, adding Members, pending invitations, unverified emails, last Owner, Role checks (403), isolation (404 identical to a missing Workspace on every endpoint, Contacts through another Workspace's path, search, Tags, Duplicates and Export of another Workspace), Contact create, rejections leave nothing, trimming, Slovenian characters, version conflict (409), delete and Restore, Attributes, Tags, Tag rename and delete, search (diacritics), filters, paging, Revisions and Restore of a Revision, immutable Revisions, Duplicate sets (email, phone, name, transitive), duplicate warning, Merge, Export (selection, filter, columns, text cells), purge, Workspace deletion. R32: rate limit | every run |
| Feature `import` | I01–I13: valid import, Export → import round trip, header matching, cells and Tags, all or nothing, row rule, invalid and duplicate headers, unreadable / empty / too large workbook, formula cell, Revisions, duplicate report, Roles, Slovenian characters | runs whose features include `import` |
| Feature `activity` | A01–A14: order and authors, names as of the Revision, delete and Restore, Merge, Tag rename, filters by author, change type, Contact and combined, paging, invalid parameters, purge, isolation, Viewer | runs whose features include `activity` |

Users are created in the emulator through its REST API, with verified emails; every generated name is letters only with a random tag, and every scenario creates its own Workspaces, so earlier data never disturbs the checks. UI-only criteria (the pages, the Slovenian texts, accessibility) are not checked by the oracle; the run's own frozen tests and phase 6 cover them. Standard library only (Python 3.10+).

## One command

```bash
python3 <this folder>/run.py <run folder>
```

It reads Run label and Features from the run's `run-config.md`, stops every stack started from the run's `02_output/docker-compose.yml`, starts the stack (the compose file's own Auth emulator, rate limit 10000), runs the base project and **every listed feature**, restarts it with rate limit 3 for R32, summarizes, stops it with `down -v`, keeps the results in `oracle-results/<run label>/` next to the run folder, copies them to `03_statistics/results/oracle/` and rebuilds the report. "harness" means the oracle could not set a scenario up (for example the emulator refused to create a User); it counts as not passed and is reported as is. Report results as they are: do not fix the run's code, and note any manual step (for example a setting the compose file did not pass through) in the run's notes.

```bash
export FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=demo-kontakti
RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=10000 docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build --force-recreate --wait

python3 $O/oracle.py ratelimit --feature <same> --out "$R/oracle-ratelimit.json"

```

Then copy the three result files to `<run folder>/03_statistics/results/oracle/` and rebuild the report in the run folder: `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics --no-backup`.

## Privacy check before committing statistics

The transcript backup (`03_statistics/data/*.jsonl`) is committed with the run and contains everything the session printed. If the agent ever printed a value from `.env`, it would be published. Before every statistics or oracle commit, in the run folder (Git Bash or Linux), list the files that contain a `.env` value of 6 or more characters; it prints names only, never values:

```bash
for k in $(sed -n 's/^\([A-Z_]*\)=.*/\1/p' .env); do v="$(sed -n "s/^$k=//p" .env | tr -d '\r')"; [ ${#v} -ge 6 ] || continue; for f in $(git ls-files -co --exclude-standard); do grep -qF -- "$v" "$f" && echo "$f contains $k"; done; done
```

`FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` (`demo-kontakti`), `FIREBASE_WEB_API_KEY` (`demo-api-key`) and `FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN` (`localhost`) are not secrets and appear in the inputs on purpose: a file listed only for these keys is fine. A file listed for `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `NVD_API_KEY`: replace the value in that committed copy with `[REDACTED]` (never in the original session file under `~/.claude`), check the file is still valid, note it in the commit message and the run notes. Closing the run's session later rebuilds the report and copies the original transcript back into `data/`; do not commit that change, discard it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Hidden oracle of the contacts feature experiment: black-box checks of a finished run through the fixed API
(`02_design/api-contract.md`) and the Firebase Auth Emulator. Never show this file to a run's agent.

Scenario groups:
  R  regression: the base project (every run: normal, greenfield and brownfield)
  I  feature `import`     (runs whose features include import)
  A  feature `activity`   (runs whose features include activity)
A new feature is one function `feature_<name>(ctx)` with its own scenario letter, added to FEATURES at the end of this file.

Phases (restart the backend with the listed settings before each phase):
  main       RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=10000   -> R01..R31 and the features' scenarios
  ratelimit  RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE=3       -> R32 (the 4th request of one User to one endpoint in a minute gets 429)

Settings (environment variables):
  ORACLE_BASE_URL      backend URL                       default http://127.0.0.1:8080
  ORACLE_AUTH_URL      Firebase Auth Emulator URL        default http://127.0.0.1:9099
  FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID  the run's project id (from .env)  default demo-kontakti

Usage: python3 oracle.py <main|ratelimit> --feature <none|import|activity|import,activity> [--out <file.json>]
Usually started by run.py, which reads the features from the run's run-config.md.
Standard library only (Python 3.10+). Users are created in the emulator; every name the oracle generates is letters
only and carries a random tag, and every scenario works in Workspaces it creates itself, so earlier data never
disturbs the checks.
"""
import base64, io, json, os, random, re, string, sys, time, urllib.error, urllib.parse, urllib.request, uuid, zipfile
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape

BASE = os.environ.get("ORACLE_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8080").rstrip("/")
AUTH_URL = os.environ.get("ORACLE_AUTH_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:9099").rstrip("/")
PROJECT = os.environ.get("FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID") or "demo-kontakti"
IDT = AUTH_URL + "/identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1"
TAG = "".join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(6))   # letters only
FIELDS = ["firstName", "lastName", "email", "phone", "company", "jobTitle", "street", "postalCode", "city", "country", "note"]
EXPORT_FIXED = ["id"] + FIELDS + ["tags"]
R = {}


class Harness(Exception):
    """The oracle could not set up a scenario (emulator unreachable, a prerequisite call failed): reported as 'harness'."""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
def letters(n=6):
    """A unique letters-only word, e.g. for a last name."""
    return TAG + "".join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(n))


def http(method, path, body=None, token=None, headers=None, base=BASE, raw=False, data=None):
    if body is not None:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(base + path, data=data, method=method)
    if body is not None:
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if token:
        req.add_header("Authorization", "Bearer " + token)
    for k, v in (headers or {}).items():
        req.add_header(k, v)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
            content, status, ctype = r.read(), r.status, r.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        content, status, ctype = e.read(), e.code, e.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        return 0, None, str(e.reason)
    if raw:
        return status, content, ctype
    try:
        return status, json.loads(content) if content else None, ctype
    except ValueError:
        return status, None, ctype


def api(method, path, user=None, body=None, **kw):
    st, js, _ = http(method, path, body=body, token=user.token if user else None, **kw)
    return st, js


def error_fields(js):
    return {e.get("field") for e in (js or {}).get("errors", []) if isinstance(e, dict)}


def record(sc, result, detail):
    R[sc] = {"result": result if isinstance(result, str) else ("pass" if result else "fail"), "detail": detail}
    print(f"{sc:5s} {R[sc]['result']:7s} {detail}")


def scenario(sc, fn, *args):
    """Run one scenario; a Harness error is 'harness', any other crash is a 'fail' with the reason."""

> Written in: phase 7 · Source: `run-log.json` · Agent: writes

Write the tables from `run-log.json`; no estimates. The summary answers three questions: what did the run cost in agent time and money, what did it deliver, and what held it back.
